summary: A rule of the project's own ArchUnit tests
why: The project writes ArchUnit rules as tests named `*ArchTest` or `*ArchitectureTest`; nitpicker runs them and reports each violated rule by the name of its test field or method.
allowed: Fix the code the rule's message names.

why: One of nitpicker's own architecture rules, run with ArchUnit over the compiled classes of a Spring project: it keeps the package-by-feature layout and the layering of the TypeScript preset.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: A controller holds or creates another controller: a field, constructor or method parameter of that type, also inside a generic, or `new OtherController()`.
allowed: Move what both controllers need into a service both call: a controller handles its own requests and does not hold another controller.

why: One of nitpicker's own architecture rules, run with ArchUnit over the compiled classes of a Spring project: it keeps the package-by-feature layout and the layering of the TypeScript preset.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: A request-mapping method of a controller takes or returns an `@Entity` type, also inside a generic.
allowed: Take and return a record (DTO) in the controller and map it in the service.

why: One of nitpicker's own architecture rules, run with ArchUnit over the compiled classes of a Spring project: it keeps the package-by-feature layout and the layering of the TypeScript preset.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: A controller depends on a repository or on data access directly (`JdbcTemplate`, `EntityManager`, `DataSource` and the like).
allowed: Have the controller call a service that uses the repository: controllers call services only.

why: One of nitpicker's own architecture rules, run with ArchUnit over the compiled classes of a Spring project: it keeps the package-by-feature layout and the layering of the TypeScript preset.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: A class uses a class from a sub-package of another feature; only the classes directly in a feature's package are its public face. When a layering rule reports the same class and dependency, only the layering finding is shown, unless an exception lifts it.
allowed: Use only the classes directly in the other feature's package, or move what both need to `<root>.shared`.

why: One of nitpicker's own architecture rules, run with ArchUnit over the compiled classes of a Spring project: it keeps the package-by-feature layout and the layering of the TypeScript preset.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: A class sits directly in the root package, or in a root sub-package named for a layer (controller, service, repository, entity, dto, util, common, web, api, domain, adapter and the like).
allowed: Package by feature: put the class in `<root>.<feature>` with that feature's controller, service and repository, and pure utilities in `<root>.shared`.

why: One of nitpicker's own architecture rules, run with ArchUnit over the compiled classes of a Spring project: it keeps the package-by-feature layout and the layering of the TypeScript preset.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: A test class or method has `@DirtiesContext`.
allowed: Reset the state in the test itself, or test the class without a Spring context.

why: One of nitpicker's own architecture rules, run with ArchUnit over the compiled classes of a Spring project: it keeps the package-by-feature layout and the layering of the TypeScript preset.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: A repository depends on a `@Service`: a field, parameter, return type or call.
allowed: Have the service call the repository and pass it what it needs: a repository only reads and writes data and depends on no service.

why: One of nitpicker's own architecture rules, run with ArchUnit over the compiled classes of a Spring project: it keeps the package-by-feature layout and the layering of the TypeScript preset.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: A singleton bean takes a request-, session-, `websocket`-, Spring Batch `step`- or `job`-scoped bean without a scoped proxy.
allowed: Inject `ObjectProvider<T>` and call `getObject()` per use, or give the scoped bean a scoped proxy (`proxyMode = ScopedProxyMode.TARGET_CLASS`).

why: One of nitpicker's own architecture rules, run with ArchUnit over the compiled classes of a Spring project: it keeps the package-by-feature layout and the layering of the TypeScript preset.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: A `@Service` or repository depends on the web layer: a controller, `ResponseEntity`, or servlet and Spring web types.
allowed: Take and return plain values, throw a domain exception for errors, and map them to web types in the controller or a `@ControllerAdvice`.

why: One of nitpicker's own architecture rules, run with ArchUnit over the compiled classes of a Spring project: it keeps the package-by-feature layout and the layering of the TypeScript preset.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: A class in `shared` is a Spring bean or an `@Entity`, or depends on a class of another root package.
allowed: Keep `shared` to pure utilities; move a bean or an entity to the feature that owns it.

why: One of nitpicker's own architecture rules, run with ArchUnit over the compiled classes of a Spring project: it keeps the package-by-feature layout and the layering of the TypeScript preset.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: A test that starts a Spring context sits in the unit test source set and is not an integration test by the slow-test rule.
allowed: Test the class with `new` and mocks, or run it as an integration test: name it `*IT` or put it in an integration test source set; a package named `integration` or `it` also counts.

summary: An inline suppression of the tool
why: A suppression annotation hides a finding from the report, so a source scan reports every one.
allowed: Do not silence Error Prone inline: fix the finding.

summary: A file is not formatted
why: The Java presets keep one layout, the formatter's. google-java-format runs in check mode and reports every file it would change.
allowed: Run google-java-format on the file; it fixes the layout.

summary: A file is not formatted
why: The Java presets keep one layout, the formatter's. palantir-java-format runs in check mode and reports every file it would change.
allowed: Run palantir-java-format on the file; it fixes the layout.

summary: An inline suppression of the tool
why: A suppression annotation hides a finding from the report, so a source scan reports every one.
allowed: Do not silence PMD inline: fix the finding.

summary: An inline suppression of the tool
why: A suppression annotation hides a finding from the report, so a source scan reports every one.
allowed: Do not silence SpotBugs inline: fix the bug.

why: Nitpicker reads the Spring configuration files of a Spring project (`application.properties`, `application.yml` and their profile variants) for settings that are unsafe outside a test or local profile.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: `spring.profiles.active` or `spring.profiles.include` has a literal value in the main (profile-less) document.
allowed: Set the active profile from the environment (`SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE`), not in the packaged file: it turns those profiles on in every environment.

why: Nitpicker reads the Spring configuration files of a Spring project (`application.properties`, `application.yml` and their profile variants) for settings that are unsafe outside a test or local profile.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: An actuator endpoint is exposed to the web beyond what is safe: `*`, a sensitive endpoint, unrestricted access, or the shutdown or heapdump endpoint open.
allowed: Expose only the endpoints the operation needs (`health`, `info`) and keep the sensitive ones restricted.

why: Nitpicker reads the Spring configuration files of a Spring project (`application.properties`, `application.yml` and their profile variants) for settings that are unsafe outside a test or local profile.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto` or `spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto` is neither `none` nor `validate`, or `spring.jpa.generate-ddl` is true.
allowed: Manage the schema with Flyway or Liquibase and set the mode to `none` or `validate`.

why: Nitpicker reads the Spring configuration files of a Spring project (`application.properties`, `application.yml` and their profile variants) for settings that are unsafe outside a test or local profile.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: `server.error.include-stacktrace`, `include-message` or `include-binding-errors` is `always` or `on-param`, or `include-exception` is true.
allowed: Set `server.error.include-message=never` and return a fixed `ProblemDetail` from a `@RestControllerAdvice`.

why: Nitpicker reads the Spring configuration files of a Spring project (`application.properties`, `application.yml` and their profile variants) for settings that are unsafe outside a test or local profile.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: A literal value under a key that names a secret (`password`, `secret`, `token`, `api-key` and the like), or a URL that carries a credential.
allowed: Supply the secret from the environment (a placeholder without a default) or a secret store.

why: Nitpicker reads the Spring configuration files of a Spring project (`application.properties`, `application.yml` and their profile variants) for settings that are unsafe outside a test or local profile.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: `@Scheduled`, `@Async`, a cache annotation, `@PreAuthorize` or `@Retryable` is used while no main class has the matching `@Enable...` annotation.
allowed: Add the matching `@Enable...` annotation to a configuration class, or remove the annotation that does nothing without it.

why: Nitpicker reads the Spring configuration files of a Spring project (`application.properties`, `application.yml` and their profile variants) for settings that are unsafe outside a test or local profile.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: JPA is used in the main sources and `spring.jpa.open-in-view` is unset or true.
allowed: Set `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false`: the default holds a database connection through view rendering and hides N+1 queries.

why: Nitpicker reads the Spring configuration files of a Spring project (`application.properties`, `application.yml` and their profile variants) for settings that are unsafe outside a test or local profile.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: `spring.main.allow-circular-references`, `allow-bean-definition-overriding` or `lazy-initialization` is true.
allowed: Remove the flag and restructure the beans: it hides wiring problems instead of fixing them.

why: Nitpicker reads the Spring configuration files of a Spring project (`application.properties`, `application.yml` and their profile variants) for settings that are unsafe outside a test or local profile.
scope: A project with Spring on the compile classpath.
summary: SQL logging, Hibernate bind logging at TRACE, the H2 console, or an actuator endpoint that shows values or details is on.
allowed: Turn the diagnostic off in the packaged configuration; enable it only in a local or test profile.

summary: A test class that no Test task or Failsafe execution runs.
why: A test that never runs cannot fail, so it proves nothing.
allowed: Register a Test task for its source set (Gradle), or bind the integration-test and verify goals of maven-failsafe-plugin (Maven), so that it runs.
